distractors.reason: 'Appeal to' means try to win support or sympathy. It describes a goal, not a last-resort strategy.
'Refer to' means mention or point to something. It does not describe turning to a method under pressure.
'Turn to' means seek help or go to someone. It is not the phrase for using a method reluctantly.

example_sentence: When logic failed, the debater had to ___ to emotion.
l1_interference: English speakers may use 'appeal to' for any use of emotion; 'resort to' signals reluctance or desperation.
common_mistake: appeal to (when the speaker has no other option)
explanation: 'Resort to' means to use a method, often an extreme one, because other options have failed. In rhetoric, it signals that a speaker has run out of logical arguments.

related_collocations.example: The advert appeals to emotion rather than facts.
When the data failed, they fell back on old models.
She turned to the audience for support.

memory_tip: RESORT TO = use a last-choice method | APPEAL TO = seek sympathy, REFER TO = mention
